title: Labeling and analyzing lipid droplets in mouse muscle stem cells
protocol: Trypsinize myoblasts prior to staining.
Plate myoblasts onto culture vessels of choice.
Seed 6 × 10^4 myoblasts per well in a 24-well plate for staining 24-48 hours later.
Consider using chamber slides or coverglass to eliminate auto-fluorescence and improve signaling specificity.
Coat positively charged glass coverslips with Matrigel to provide extracellular matrix for myoblast attachment and proliferation.
Sterilize coverslips by autoclaving in aluminum foil.
Unwrap the sterilized slide and place the coverslip into a 6-well culture plate in a cell culture hood using hygiene practices.
Dilute Matrigel in DMEM medium at a 1:10 ratio.
Add approximately 1 mL of the diluted Matrigel to cover the entire coverslip.
Allow the Matrigel to sit for about 30 minutes at room temperature.
Remove excess Matrigel and leave the coverslip to dry for about 20 minutes in the cell culture hood.
Dilute 40,000 myoblasts in 200 μL of culture medium (F-10 Ham’s nutrient mix, 7.5% horse serum, 20% Fetal Bovine Serum, 4 ng/mL basic Fibroblast growth factor, 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Add the myoblast solution dropwise to the coated coverslip.
Place the 6-well culture plate in a 5% CO2 cell culture incubator and check the cell status the next day.
Submerge the entire coverslip with enough medium if myoblasts have attached to prevent drying.
Dilute BODIPY (1:1,000) directly in the culture medium.
Rock the plate gently so that BODIPY spreads evenly in the medium.
Incubate the plate for 30 min at 37°C in the cell culture incubator.
Take care to avoid exposing the culture plate to light.
Wrap the culture plate in aluminum foil for transportation from the culture room to the dark room.
At the desired time point, take out the cell culture plate and transfer the coverslip with tweezers.
Blot away excessive medium under and around the staining area using Kimwipes.
Draw a boundary on the slide with a hydrophobic pen.
Fix the slide with 4% PFA for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the medium off myoblasts on chamber slides or plates/dishes.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 3 times.
Fix myoblasts on chamber slides or plates/dishes with 4% PFA for 10 min.
Wash fixed myoblasts with 1× PBS 3 times.
Quench residual PFA with 100 mM Glycine for 10 min.
Wash myoblasts another 3 times with 1× PBS.
Block cells with blocking buffer for at least 1 h at RT.
Dilute PAX7 antibody in blocking buffer at a ratio determined empirically.
Incubate the diluted PAX7 antibody with myoblasts overnight in the cold room (4°C).
Wash the myoblasts with 1× PBST containing 0.1% Tween-20 for three times, each time for 5 minutes.
Prepare Alexa 568 goat anti-mouse IgG1 against PAX7, BODIPY and DAPI mixture in 1× PBST.
Stain the myoblasts with the prepared mixture for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark room.
Wash the myoblasts with 1× PBST for three times, each time for 5 minutes.
Mount the slides with mounting media.
Seal the slides with nail polish and let dry before imaging.
Isolate myofibers based on the published protocol.
Resuspend isolated single myofibers in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium supplemented with 20% Fetal Bovine Serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 4 ng/mL basic fibroblast growth factor.
Split the resuspended myofibers into three parts.
Transfer two parts of myofibers to two 6-cm horse serum coated culture dishes.
Rock the plates gently so that the myofibers are spread evenly in the dishes.
Culture the myofibers for 48 hours or 72 hours as needed.
Collect the myofiber immediately in 4% PFA by transferring it to a well containing approximately 500 μL of 4% PFA in a 48-well plate.
Transfer single myofibers from the culture to empty wells containing 500 μL 4% PFA in a 48-well plate using a large-cut Pasteur pipette.
Replace with fresh 4% PFA if excessive medium is transferred during collection.
Fix the myofibers and wash with 1× PBS for 3 times.
Remove medium/PFA mixture after fibers settle to the bottom of the well under dissecting microscope.
Add 500 μL fresh 4% PFA and fix for 10 min at room temperature if too much medium is transferred.
Wash myofibers with 1× PBS for 3 times post-fixation adjustment.
Store myofiber at 4°C until all fibers are collected.
Quench residual PFA with 500 μL of 100 mM Glycine for 10 min at room temperature in myofibers from different time points.
Wash the myofibers with 1× PBS for 3 times after quenching.
Block the myofibers with blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
Dilute PAX7 and MyoD antibodies.
Stain myofibers overnight at 4°C.
Wash myofibers three times with 1× PBST for 5 minutes each.
Incubate myofibers with secondary antibody (anti-mouse IgG1-568 for PAX7, anti-mouse IgG2b-647 for MyoD), DAPI for nuclei, and BODIPY for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash myofibers three times with 1× PBST.
Pre-wet the central region of a positively charged glass slide with 1× PBST.
Transfer myofibers to the pre-wetted slide using a large-bore Pasteur pipette, avoiding excess liquid on the slide.
Remove remaining 1× PBST from the slide using a fine-cut Pasteur pipette.
Add mounting medium onto the slide.
Separate intertwined myofibers into individual myofibers with two 30-G syringe needles.
Cover the slide with a coverglass at a 30-degree angle, touching one edge to the slide and gradually lowering it until flat.
Blot excess mounting medium from the slide using Kimwipes.
Seal the slide with nail polish.
Cover the coverglass slowly and carefully to prevent bubble formation and myofiber movement.
Visualize myofibers under the microscope.
Prepare muscle-derived single cell suspension before sorting.
Use CD45, CD31, and SCA-1 as negative selection markers for hematopoietic, endothelial, and mesenchymal cells respectively.
Use VCAM-1 (CD106) as a positive selection marker for MuSCs.
Ensure fluorophore used for antigen staining does not overlap with BODIPY or LipidSpot fluorophores.
Test stability of BODIPY signals during washing and sorting steps in your system.
Use far-red fluorophore LipidSpot for FACS-based applications to maintain signal stability.
Sort MuSCs by BD-FACS Aria III FACS system into FACS wash medium (HAM’S F-10 medium supplemented with 10% Horse Serum, 1% P/S).
Perform BODIPY/LipidSpot610 non-stained control by aliquoting a small volume of the sorted MuSCs.
Analyze the non-stained control cells first to establish the threshold of the BODIPY non-stained sample at 503 nm or LipidSpot610 non-stained sample at 638 nm.
Stain the remaining cells with BODIPY/LipidSpot610 as described below.
Centrifuge the MuSCs at 4°C at 2,500 rpm (∼600 g) for 5 min.
Resuspend the MuSCs with 1× PBS and then stain with BODIPY/LipidSpot610 at RT for 30 min.
Wash with 1× PBS again before analyzing the MuSCs with the FACS sorter again.
Gate different intensities of the BODIPY/LipidSpot610 signals into low, medium and high respectively.
Sort cells based on the BODIPY/LipidSpot610 signals.

Plate LDLow and LDHigh sorted MuSCs onto Matrigel coated plates to examine their proliferative and differentiation potentials or inject them into muscle-injured immune-deficient mice to assess their regenerative capacities.
Take out the culture dish from the incubator and immediately wash with ice-cold 1× PBS once.
Aspirate excess 1× PBS quickly and add 2 mL of TEM fixation buffer.
Aspirate TEM buffer off and replace with 1.5 mL of fresh TEM buffer.
Incubate myoblasts for 5 min on the plate for initial fixation.
Scrape myoblasts carefully from the culture dish using a cell scraper.
Collect myoblasts in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Conduct this step on ice for better preservation of ultrastructure such as mitochondria.
Store myoblasts at 4°C until TEM sample processing.
Perform cervical dislocation to sacrifice the mouse quickly.
Pinch the toes to ensure the death of the mouse before procedures.
Remove the skin with surgical scissors and expose the TA muscle.
Add two drops of fixative to the muscle before dissecting.
Dissect the TA muscle out from the mouse.
Cut the distal tendon first during dissection.
Take care not to stretch the muscle too much to avoid damaging the sarcomeres.
Transfer the TA muscle to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 mL of fixative to the Eppendorf tube containing the TA muscle.
Trim the TA muscle along its long axis to reduce its width to about 5–10 mm.
Store the trimmed TA muscle at 4°C until ready for TEM sample processing.
